summary: The mechanism is real, but it is smaller than the hypothesis says now that master aligns over 32 experts: about 45K dead CTAs, not 66K. The 3-5% kernel-row target is also smaller than this row's run-to-run noise (7463-9174 us for near-identical code). Run it, but with an in-process paired graph-timed A/B of master's kernel against the persistent kernel at T=16384 logged from prepare(). Without that, the single result cannot be read.
justification: A. The mechanism is plausible: at BLOCK_T 256 the w13 variant (254-255 regs x 256 threads, ~140 KB smem) fits one CTA per SM, so dead CTAs retire one after another per SM. But the hypothesis was written against 635cfee (align over 257 buckets). On master (stack-tonight-five) moe_align_block_size runs over LOCAL_EXPERTS=32: ~545 token tiles at T=16384, ~448 of them the -1 bucket, ~80 local, ~17 past n_padded. That leaves ~465 dead token tiles: ~29.8K dead w13 CTAs and ~14.9K dead w2 CTAs (zero-store OFF on master, so pure returns), ~45K total, ~340 per SM. At ~1 us each that is ~0.3 ms, 3-4% of the 8.1-9.2 ms row, so -3 to -5% on first_turn and ~+1% headline is the upper bound. The persistent loop does not make a dead tile free: each still pays a dependent load of expert_ids[pid_t], and master's body loads sorted_ids before the -1 branch, so the real saving may be about half. Calibration: moe-align-32-experts-first-turn removed ~21K dead CTAs and the four first_turn kernel rows did not move outside noise. Kernel-row noise across same-code runs is ~+-10%. Build notes: (1) load expert_ids first and move the sorted_ids/offs_token load inside the live branch; better, prefetch the next tile's expert id at the loop top. (2) w13 BLOCK_T 256 already spills 4 at 254 regs; log n_regs/n_spills for both variants vs master. (3) Tail imbalance 2-3%, acceptable. (4) GROUP_SIZE_T swizzle with runtime num_pid_t and a strided loop keeps L2 reuse.
confounders: moe-align-32-experts-first-turn (in stack-tonight-five): already removed ~224 past-n_padded tiles, so the prize is ~45K dead CTAs, not 66K. Arithmetic; no A/B needed.
w2-nonlocal-zero-store-off-first-turn (in stack-tonight-five): w2 -1 tiles are pure returns, so the loop saves only their launch cost; read the '[w2 zero-store]' log line.
experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 / experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: BLOCK_T 256 forces one CTA per SM, which is the premise; master's config, fixed, not a confounder.
router-hilo-one-gemm-n512, moe-align-local-routes-parallel-port, silu-mul-triton-local-rows-marlin-turn: separate kernels; no confound.
interference: No companion makes this readable; the ambiguity is kernel-row noise (~+-10%). Fix it in the run itself: in prepare() (untimed), build realistic T=16384 routing (random distinct top-8 of 256 mapped to 32 local, as _check_experts_e2e does), align with moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 256, LOCAL_EXPERTS), then time CUDA-graph replays of master's non-persistent kernel and the persistent kernel, w13 and w2 each, interleaved over >=5 alternations with cold L2, and log per-GEMM medians and their ratio. That paired ratio is the readout; the judged headline is a sanity check. Optionally gate the persistent path ON only at ratio <= 0.98 (shape-class decision from synthetic data). Overlap: experts-cuda-wgmma-grouped-gemm-remeasure-sm90a-inproc (running) replaces this kernel at first_turn; first-turn-moe-dead-work-stack and experts-triton-turn4-persistent-local-align (queued) contain this change, so do not count them as independent evidence.
rules_flags: None blocking. NUM_SMS from device properties is a hardware constant; n_padded is read on device; precision unchanged.
A prepare()-time timing gate must use synthetic data, depend only on shape class, and add no work inside kernel_fn.
Keep _check_expert_gemms' -1 block and past-n_padded assertions; add a check case with tiles > NUM_SMS (e.g. 2*NUM_SMS live tiles) so the strided loop wrap is exercised.
open_questions: Where does sgl-kernel's align place the -1 bucket? If contiguous, a follow-up could loop over live tiles only.
Does the persistent loop change Triton's inner-K pipelining or add spills to w13 BLOCK_T 256?
Should the next-tile expert_id prefetch be part of this change?
If the CUDA wgmma remeasure wins at first_turn, this becomes moot.
